explanations: Correct. f(5) calls f(int) because 5 is an int; f(5.0) calls f(double) because 5.0 is a double.

questions.question:
Is this overloading valid?
static int sumar(int a, int b)
static double sumar(int a, int b)
options: Yes, because they return different types
No, because the parameters are identical
It depends on the Java version
explanations: The return type does not determine overloading.
Correct. You cannot overload by changing only the return type.
Static does not affect the validity of overloading.
This rule is the same in all versions.

questions.question: What does procesar(3.14f) call if procesar(int) and procesar(double) exist?
explanations: float is not converted to int directly.
Correct. float is promoted to double (the closest conversion in the hierarchy).
There is no error; there is a valid conversion.
There is no float method, but double accepts the promotion.
